hook: The House Dickens Dreamed of as a Boy
text: When Charles Dickens was a small boy in Kent, he used to stop on the road at Gad's Hill and gaze at a handsome red-brick house. His father told him that if he worked very hard, he might one day live in a house like that. Forty years later, the house came up for sale. Dickens, now famous all over the world, bought it. He wrote many of his last pages there, among the trees. And it was there, on a summer evening in eighteen seventy, that he died.
